hero.desc: Generate Veo 3.1 videos from text prompts or image anchors with native audio, first/last-frame steering, 4/6/8 second timing, and 720p or 1080p output. Choose Lite, Fast, or Quality for product demos, social ads, cinematic transitions, storyboard beats, and sound-led short clips.

modelIntro.title: What Is Veo 3.1 AI Video Generator?
description: Veo 3.1 is Google's video generation model family for creating short, realistic clips from text and image inputs. Its strongest creation controls are native audio, first-and-last-frame image guidance, reference-image direction, and cinematic prompt following.

On Toolaze, Veo 3.1 is available as Lite, Fast, and Quality model choices inside the browser video generator. Use it when the ending frame, sound cue, product reveal, camera move, or storyboard transition matters more than a generic one-shot draft.

metrics.label: Creation modes
metrics.value: Text-to-video and image-to-video with first/last-frame steering for image-based generation.

metrics.label: Image guidance
metrics.value: Toolaze supports up to two image anchors for first-frame and optional last-frame control.

metrics.label: Reference images
metrics.value: The live Toolaze generator uses first/last-frame anchors; broader Veo 3.1 reference-image modes can use up to three images where that option is available.

metrics.label: Native audio
metrics.value: Veo 3.1 can generate synchronized ambience, effects, speech-style cues, and sound-led scene detail from the prompt.

metrics.label: Duration
metrics.value: Toolaze exposes 4, 6, or 8 second outputs for Veo 3.1.

metrics.label: Resolution
metrics.value: 720p or 1080p output on Toolaze. Google lists 4K for some Veo 3.1 options, but the visible Toolaze generator uses 720p and 1080p.

metrics.label: Credits
metrics.value: Lite starts at 30 Credits, Fast at 60 Credits, and Quality at 450 Credits for 720p output.

howToUse.title: How to Use Veo 3.1 on Toolaze

steps.title: Choose a Veo 3.1 model
steps.desc: Select Veo 3.1 Lite for low-cost tests, Fast for balanced iteration, or Quality when fidelity is worth the higher Credit cost.

steps.title: Pick text or image input
steps.desc: Start from a prompt for text-to-video, or switch to image-to-video when a first frame or first-and-last-frame transition should anchor the clip.

steps.title: Write motion and sound together
steps.desc: Describe subject action, camera movement, lighting, textures, dialogue or sound effects, and the final beat in one clear prompt.

steps.title: Set output and generate
steps.desc: Choose 16:9, 9:16, or Auto, select 4, 6, or 8 seconds, pick 720p or 1080p, then review the Credit requirement before generation.

promptExamples.title: Veo 3.1 Prompt Examples
promptExamples.subtitle: Copy these prompts when you need first/last-frame control, product motion, native audio, or cinematic social clips.

items.title: Product Reveal with Native Audio
items.prompt: A cinematic product reveal for a matte black espresso machine on a marble counter. Slow push-in, steam curls from the cup, chrome edges catch soft morning light, the final frame holds on the logo plate. Add synchronized espresso hiss, cup contact, and quiet room ambience.
items.description: Combines product detail, camera direction, final hold, and native sound cues.

items.title: First and Last Frame Transition
items.prompt: Animate from the uploaded first frame of a closed perfume box to the uploaded last frame of the bottle standing beside unfolded packaging. Keep the camera locked, preserve the brand colors, let the lid open naturally, add soft paper movement and a subtle whoosh into the final pose.
items.description: Uses first and last frame control to prevent the reveal from drifting.

items.title: Storyboard Beat for Social Ads
items.prompt: Shot 1: a runner ties bright shoes at sunrise. Shot 2: close-up of the sole hitting wet pavement. Shot 3: side tracking shot through city reflections. Shot 4: final hero frame with the shoes stopped beside a glowing storefront. Add footsteps, fabric movement, and distant traffic.
items.description: Structures a short ad as timed shots with sound and a final brand moment.

items.title: Cinematic Interior Mood Clip
items.prompt: A quiet boutique hotel lobby at blue hour, camera glides past brass lamps and textured walls toward a rain-streaked window. Warm light reflects on polished stone, curtains move slightly, and the scene ends on a calm seating area with soft rain and low piano ambience.
items.description: Shows Veo 3.1 as a mood and ambience generator, not only a product tool.

tips.title: Control the landing frame
tips.text:
Weak prompt: Make this product box open dramatically.
Better prompt: Start from the uploaded closed box frame, open the lid in one smooth motion, keep the box shape and label stable, and land exactly on the uploaded final frame with the bottle upright beside the packaging.

tips.title: Write sound as action
tips.text:
Weak prompt: Add good audio.
Better prompt: Add synchronized espresso steam hiss, ceramic cup contact, soft counter taps, and a quiet room tone that follows the product reveal without overpowering it.

tips.title: Keep the sequence short
tips.text:
Weak prompt: Show many scenes of a full commercial.
Better prompt: Use four concise beats: establishing shot, tactile close-up, main motion, final hold. Keep the camera movement smooth and the subject consistent.

faq.q: What is Veo 3.1 AI Video Generator?
faq.a: Veo 3.1 is Google's AI video model family for generating short clips from text prompts or image anchors with native audio and stronger frame control.

faq.q: Does Veo 3.1 support first and last frames?
faq.a: Yes. Veo 3.1 supports first-and-last-frame generation. On Toolaze, use image-to-video and the First/Last Frames option when the start and ending composition should be controlled.

faq.q: How many reference images can I use?
faq.a: Toolaze supports up to two image anchors for Veo 3.1 first/last-frame generation. Veo 3.1 reference-image modes can use up to three images where that option is available.
Yes. Veo 3.1 can create native synchronized audio such as ambience, object sounds, speech-style cues, and sound effects from the prompt.

faq.q: What duration does Toolaze support for Veo 3.1?
faq.a: Toolaze exposes 4, 6, and 8 second Veo 3.1 outputs.
Toolaze exposes 720p and 1080p for Veo 3.1. Some Google surfaces mention 4K, but use the visible Toolaze controls as the source of truth for this generator.

faq.q: What is the difference between Veo 3.1 Lite, Fast, and Quality?
faq.a: Lite is the cheapest option for quick tests, Fast is the balanced iteration option, and Quality is the highest-cost option for stronger fidelity review.

faq.q: How many Credits does Veo 3.1 cost?
faq.a: Veo 3.1 Lite starts at 30 Credits, Fast starts at 60 Credits, and Quality starts at 450 Credits for 720p output. The generator updates the requirement before generation.
Veo 3.1 video generation depends on available Credits, account state, selected model tier, resolution, and duration. Check the visible Credit requirement before generation.

faq.q: When should I choose Veo 3.1 instead of Kling, Wan, or Seedance?
faq.a: Choose Veo 3.1 when native audio and first/last-frame control are the priority. Choose Kling for stronger action, Wan for Wan-family transitions, and Seedance for reference-heavy scene planning.
